annotation.providersSubtitle: Save multiple provider configurations; switch between them with a click. The active one is used when you annotate assets.
annotation.noProviders: No providers yet. Add one to enable annotation.
annotation.behaviorSubtitle: Settings below apply to whichever provider is active when you annotate.
annotation.autoOnImportHint: Off by default. When on, every imported asset is annotated as part of the import pipeline.
annotation.tagLanguagesHint: Both selected means each photo gets tags in both languages, so search hits across users.
annotation.maxTagsHint: Hard cap. The model sees this and trims its own output.
annotation.maxDescLengthHint: Characters. Short captions read better in the inspector and search.
annotation.videoFrameIntervalHint: For video: sample one frame every N seconds to send to the AI. 0 = just first / middle / last (3 frames). Higher coverage for longer clips costs more tokens.
annotation.maxWorkersHint: How many API requests run in parallel during batch annotation. Higher is faster but may hit provider rate limits. 3 is a safe default.
annotation.customInstructionsHint: Appended to every prompt. Use this to bias toward your taste — e.g. "prefer style and mood tags over generic objects".
annotation.displayNameHint: Short label shown in the provider list.
annotation.hostUrlHint: Full OpenAI-compatible base URL including /v1. Local Ollama is usually http://localhost:11434/v1.
annotation.apiKeyHintLocal: Leave empty for local-only providers like Ollama.
annotation.apiKeyHint: Stored locally in your keychain. Never sent to AfterFrame servers.
annotation.restartHandlers: Restart the app to pick up the new IPC handlers.
annotation.modelHintLocal: Type the model id or click ↻ to fetch the list from your endpoint.
annotation.calloutBody: — when you annotate, AfterFrame uploads a 512px-max-edge JPEG directly from your machine to {{provider}}. We never proxy or store your photos. EXIF GPS is stripped from the upload.

library.catalogScratchHint: Unsaved working library. Create or open a catalog to persist it on disk.
library.switchCatalogHint: Open an existing .afcatalog, or create a new one. The current view reloads.
library.watchedSubtitle: Belongs only to the current Catalog. Watching switches with the Catalog, and new files in these folders are imported automatically.
library.noWatched: No watched directories in this Catalog.
library.depthMapsHint: Cached depth fields for depth-aware text. Safe to delete — regenerated on demand.
library.stickerLibraryHint: Extracted stickers and their thumbnails. Deleting removes saved stickers.
library.videoProxiesHint: H.264 versions transcoded for clips the player can't decode (e.g. 10-bit HEVC). Safe to delete — regenerated when needed.
library.lutSubtitle: For the editor's LUT tool. Shared by every catalog.
library.lutLibraryHint: Copies of the LUTs imported in the editor: {{count}}, {{size}}. Emptying moves the whole folder to the Trash; the files you imported from stay where they were.
library.clearLutsMessage: Its {{count}} LUTs go to the Trash together and can be put back from there. Added folders are not touched.
library.lutFoldersHint: The editor reads the LUTs in these folders where they are: nothing is copied, no space is used. Removing one only stops reading it; no file is deleted.
library.lutFolderUnavailable: {{path}} · can't be read: moved, renamed, or its drive isn't connected
library.removeLutFolder: Stop reading this folder (no file is deleted)
library.colorsAutoHint: New photos get their dominant colours as their previews are made (about 20 ms each); the missing ones are filled in when the library opens. Off, it only runs from the buttons below.
library.colorsHint: {{analyzed}} photos have a palette, {{missing}} do not. New photos are analysed as their previews are made; the missing ones are filled in when the library opens.
library.colorsRunning: Analysing… progress is in the activity center, top right.
library.generateHdHint: Used to view photos when the original is missing, for collage rendering, and by the AI assistant. Day-to-day viewing uses the original, so most photos never need it. Off by default — saves roughly 0.5–1 MB per photo on disk. Applies to future imports.

about.tagline: A local-first photo workspace for photographers.
about.updatesMid: — when a new version ships, download the .dmg from
about.updatesPost: and drag it over the old Applications/AfterFrame.app. Catalogs and settings persist across updates.

repaint.providersSubtitle: Image generation providers for AI Repaint. The active provider is used by the editor and by agent (MCP) repaint requests.
repaint.noProvider: No repaint provider configured yet. Add one to enable AI Repaint.

people.modelSubtitle: Runs only on this Mac. Face embeddings and person groups stay in the current catalog.
people.noModel: This build doesn't include the face model. Choose a compatible model below.
people.builtInNeedsMacOS: The built-in face model needs macOS {{version}} or later. You can still choose a compatible Core ML model below.
people.builtInModelHint: Built into AfterFrame · {{size}} · nothing to download
people.installModelHint: Optional. Choose an .afpersonmodel bundle or a compatible Core ML .mlpackage. It's validated first, then copied into AfterFrame storage.
people.autoIndexOnImportHint: Off by default. When an import finishes, new photos are analyzed in the background. Needs an installed model. You can pause it from Background Activity.
people.unverified: Custom model — review its license before distribution.
people.indexSubtitle: Runs as a low-priority background task. You can keep browsing and pause or resume it from Background Activity.
people.analyzeLibraryHint: Only images with a detected, usable face are added to the people index. Re-runs skip unchanged photos.
people.privacy: Your photos never leave this Mac. The worker detects faces and computes embeddings locally; names are not sent to any service.

providers.name: Name
providers.savedNote: Credentials saved (encrypted). Leave blank to keep existing.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.editorsSubtitle: Auto-detected photo editors available in the gallery right-click → Open With.
integrations.mcpSubtitle: AfterFrame runs a local MCP server so agents like Claude Code can search, organise and edit this library. It only accepts connections from this Mac.
integrations.mcpPortInUseHint: Port {{port}} is taken, usually by another AfterFrame window. Quit the other one and restart, or set AFTERFRAME_MCP_PORT to a free port.
integrations.mcpErrorHint: The MCP server could not start. {{error}}

json.label: Cursor and .mcp.json
json.hint: For clients that connect to HTTP servers directly.

claudeDesktop.label: Claude Desktop
claudeDesktop.hint: Add to claude_desktop_config.json. Claude Desktop needs the mcp-remote bridge, which requires Node.js.

transfer.title: Backup & transfer
transfer.subtitle: Export AI providers, API keys and common settings to a file, then import it on another computer.
transfer.importHint: Merges a .afsettings file into this computer's settings.

sections.watermarkHint: Author name, frame templates (not logo files)

transfer.includeKeysHint: Keys are encrypted with the password below. Without it, they cannot be imported.
transfer.unreadable: {{count}} keys could not be read (Keychain access denied) and were skipped
transfer.keysInFile: This file contains {{count}} keys. Enter the password set at export.
transfer.noKeysInFile: This file has no API keys. Re-enter them on this computer after importing.
transfer.mergeNote: Import merges with this computer's settings and never removes existing providers. Current settings are backed up first.
transfer.imported: Import complete. The window reloads when you click Done.
transfer.faceModelNote: Face recognition models are not transferred. Reinstall one under People if needed.

errors.weak_passphrase: Password must be at least 8 characters
errors.invalid_file: Not a valid AfterFrame settings file
errors.newer_version: This file comes from a newer AfterFrame. Update the app first
errors.expired: This import expired. Choose the file again
errors.plaintext_storage: Keychain encryption is unavailable, so keys were stored unencrypted

watermark.profileSubtitle: What frame text fills in for you. Add “Author” in the editor (Frame › Add to the frame › Photo info) or use a template that has it.
watermark.author: Author
watermark.authorHint: Your name or handle, as it should appear on photos
watermark.brandsSubtitle: Each camera's logo. A brand's is for every model of it; a model's is for that model only. Click a name to rename it: models named the same are one camera (a drone's lenses).
watermark.brandsEmpty: No photos with camera information yet.
watermark.templatesSubtitle: Saved from the editor: Frame › Templates › Save as template. Rename or duplicate them there.
watermark.deleteMessage: Photos already framed with it stay as they are.
watermark.logosSubtitle: A signature, a studio mark… for every photo: click one in the editor's Frame tool, or drag an SVG or PNG into the editor. One-colour logos are recoloured to suit. Settings export does not include logo files.
watermark.deleteLogoMessage: Templates that use it keep working, without this logo. Photos already exported are not affected.

logoErrors.too_large: Too large (SVG up to 1 MB, PNG up to 10 MB)
logoErrors.invalid_image: That file could not be read as an image
logoErrors.empty_image: There is no mark in that image
logoErrors.too_many: You already have 50 logos; delete some first
